label: live

steps.assertion: The Pro project terminal opens in its registered dedicated checkout.
The dev-madrid device terminal uses the existing relay and prints the actual remote hostname.
Type or dictate a command and Run send echo hello through the real PTY.
Sticky Ctrl and C interrupt sleep within two seconds and preserve its non-zero exit record.
Reload reconnects the same terminal and replays hello in its scrollback.
The copy buttons include exactly the requested command range and strip every escape code.

steps.assertion: Take over in browser attaches a real native thread session; leaving detaches and returns it to Jevellan.
Every captured screen passes the dedicated live vision rubric in this layout.

screens.expected: a connected project terminal with usable controls and no clipped text

cosmetic: The host/path subtitle in the header is truncated ('/Users/ggomes...'), so the full project path isn't visible there.
The rightmost key in the special-keys row is cut off at the right edge. It looks like a scrolling row, but nothing else shows that more keys are available.
Terminal output breaks words mid-word ('jevellan-l / ive-sandbox', 'jevellan-live- / sandbox %'). This is normal terminal wrapping at a narrow width but is slightly harder to read.
The 'Project' label sits alone in pink in the status row. It's unclear whether it's a tab, a link or a status badge.

screens.expected: a connected dev-madrid terminal with the remote hostname and usable controls

cosmetic: The row of special keys is cut off on the right: a partly visible button after '→' gets clipped at the screen edge. The row looks horizontally scrollable, but nothing on screen shows that more keys exist.
The first terminal line is a stray 'hostname' that appears before the prompt. It looks like local echo or a duplicated command.
There's a thin black line under the last terminal line near the bottom of the output area. It looks like a stray border or cursor rule.

screens.expected: terminal copy and Send to controls reachable at this layout

cosmetic: Header path is cut off with an ellipsis ('/Users/ggomes...').
The leftmost key in the shortcut row ('→') is partly clipped at the left edge. The row looks horizontally scrollable.
Long shell prompts wrap mid-word across two lines ('jevellan-live-' / 'sandbox %'), which makes the output harder to scan.
The 'Copied' confirmation is plain, low-emphasis text with no clear tie to the button that was pressed.

screens.expected: a browser terminal attached to a resumed native coding session, past setup and trust dialogs, with usable exit controls

cosmetic: The terminal status line is cut off at the right edge: '▸▸ bypass permissions on (shift+tab to' never finishes.
The header subtitle 'dev-madrid scenarios · /home/ggo…' is truncated, so the full project path can't be seen.
The on-screen key row (Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, arrows) is clipped on the right, with a partly visible key at the edge. It looks like it scrolls sideways.
Some terminal output lines wrap unevenly (for example 'instead / of "not found" (404)'), which suggests the terminal column count doesn't quite match the viewport width.
The session shows a stop hook error ('/bin/sh: 1: /Users/ggomes/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.0/bin/node: not found'). This is an environment problem, not a layout problem, but it's visible to the user.

observations: Usage records come from runtime-reported turn outcomes. Missing tokens or cost remain unknown; minutes include concurrent sessions.
